title: Field Service total operating model
columnSource: Columns follow Gartner's four field service scenarios.

rows.label: Cost Center
rows.description: Service exists to protect the product sale and is managed to cost.

rows.label: Profit Center
rows.description: Service is its own margin line with revenue and margin targets.

rows.label: Servitization (Outcome-based)
rows.description: Service is sold as a promised outcome rather than as labor and parts.

columns.label: Appointment-Centric
columns.description: Booked visits to a location, judged on hitting the window.

columns.label: Equipment-Centric
columns.description: Work against a serialized installed asset, judged on fixing it.

columns.label: Knowledge-Centric
columns.description: Resolution depends on expertise, often delivered remotely.

columns.label: Outcome-Centric
columns.description: The customer buys uptime, output, or usage, not the visit.

cells.oneLiner: Scheduled visits run as a cost of serving the customer.
Keeping installed equipment running as a warranty or goodwill obligation, managed to cost.
Help desk and remote support run to contain cost per resolution.
Uptime commitments carried as a cost of selling the product, not priced on their own.
Paid, booked visits such as installs and inspections, run for margin.
Service run as a margin line on a contracted installed base.
Expert and remote diagnostic services sold as a margin line.
Priced performance guarantees layered onto a margin-run service business.
Recurring subscription visits where the customer buys the schedule, not the job.
Equipment as a service: the customer pays for the asset's availability.
Subscription access to expertise, monitoring, and remote resolution.
Pay-per-outcome contracts for uptime, output, or usage.
